pulley-block-forces.alt: A pulley of mass M and radius R turns on a fixed axle hung from the ceiling. A light string wrapped around its rim holds a block of mass m, which accelerates downward with acceleration a while the pulley gains angular acceleration α, with a = Rα. Middle: the force diagram of the pulley shows the string pulling down at the rim, Earth’s gravitational force down at the center and the axle’s force up at the center; only the string’s pull has a lever arm, so F_T R = Iα. Right: the free-body diagram of the block shows the string’s tension up, shorter than Earth’s gravitational force down, so mg − F_T = ma.
